claims.text: A quality gate is a set of automated checks a change must pass before it may go further.

ci.yml@stage-2 lines 34-57: job test runs dotnet build DonHang.slnx --warnaserror then dotnet test DonHang.slnx --no-build; job app (working-directory DonHang.App) runs flutter analyze then flutter test; neither runs ./scripts/up.sh.
dotnet build with --warnaserror treats all warnings as errors, so any compiler warning fails the build.
flutter analyze runs the Dart analyzer over the project's code without running it and exits with a non-zero code when it reports issues.
claims.source_hint: Flutter/Dart docs: flutter analyze, Customizing static analysis (dart analyze exit codes)

claims.text: flutter test runs the tests in DonHang.App/test/, which at stage-2 are widget tests (testWidgets), e.g. create_order_screen_test.dart.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: Testing Flutter apps (flutter test); examples/don-hang @ stage-2 DonHang.App/test/

claims.text: At stage-2, DonHang.Tests includes integration tests that use Testcontainers to start PostgreSQL and Redis containers; the project needs Docker, not the lab (csproj comment lines 17-20).
The GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner image comes with Docker installed and running, so Testcontainers can start containers in a job without any setup step.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: GitHub-hosted runners (preinstalled software list for ubuntu-24.04: Docker); Testcontainers for .NET docs (CI)

claims.text: In the CI runs for the stage-2 commit 7a131bc (36332462105 tag stage-2, 36332055445 master), the test job's dotnet test reported Passed 24, Failed 0 for DonHang.Tests.dll (and 13 for DonHang.Samples.Tests.dll).

Each job's result is reported on the commit as its own check; test and app run as separate jobs on their own runners and both report on the same commit; ci.yml's other jobs (image, lab, k8s...) report their own checks too.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: About status checks; Using jobs in a workflow

claims.text: Blocking a merge until checks pass is a repository setting turned on by an admin: a branch protection rule or ruleset with required status checks; a pull request then merges into that branch only once every required check has passed, unless an admin bypasses the rule (by default, admins may).
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: About protected branches > Require status checks before merging; About rulesets

claims.text: Without required status checks, GitHub shows failing checks on a pull request but still allows it to be merged.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: About status checks; About protected branches
